description:
FOUND and FIXED in s470bl while shipping #1022 half (b) (the labelled bare
block is one of the shapes the dynamic-exit frame wraps, so the two arms of
_lower_bare_block had to agree).  PRE-EXISTING.

    my $x = 0; L: { $x = 1; last; $x = 2 } print "x=$x\n";
      perl:  x=1
      PCL:   Unhandled sb-int:compiled-program-error
               Form: (return-from nil nil)
               Compile-time error: return for unknown block: nil

Parser2::_lower_bare_block's UNLABELLED arm emits `(block nil (tagbody :redo
... :next))` -- the `block nil` an unlabelled `p-last` returns from.  The
LABELLED arm emitted the three loop-tag catches and no `block nil` at all, so
`(p-last)` inside it had no target.

THE WORSE SPELLING, and the reason this is not merely a loud bug: with an
enclosing loop the `(return-from nil nil)` found THAT loop's `block nil` and
exited it, silently.

    my @s; for my $i (1..3) { L: { push @s, $i; last; push @s, "X" } push @s, "after$i" }
      perl:  1 after1 2 after2 3 after3       (the `last` leaves the BARE BLOCK)
      PCL:   1                                 (it left the FOR loop)

FIX: the labelled arm gains `(block nil ...)` around the NEXT catch AND the
continue forms, so a bare `last` skips the continue block exactly as `last L`
does (probed: `L: { push @s,"b"; last } continue { push @s,"c" }` is `b` in
both, and the `next` spelling is `b c` in both).

GUARD: Pl/t/loop-exit-01.t row 19 (the nested spelling, which is the silent
one).  It is an emission change for every labelled bare block, verified over
the perl-tests corpus + the wide 1007-file population to add nothing but
`(block nil` (token-level A/B, scratch/s470bl/ab3.pl).
subject: FIXED (s470bl): a LABELLED bare block had no `(block nil ...)`, so an unlabelled `last` inside it either died at load ("return for unknown block: nil") or -- nested in a loop -- SILENTLY exited the enclosing loop instead
